title: Graduate Engineer Trainee - Electrical
summary: A graduate engineer trainee (GET) in electrical joins a power utility, EPC contractor (a firm that designs, buys and builds projects) or factory straight from college. Trainees rotate through sites and teams, supporting senior engineers with substation work, drawings, testing and commissioning before taking a permanent post.
dailyDuties: Study single line diagrams and substation layout drawings for the current project
Support testing of transformers, breakers, CTs and relays during commissioning
Check equipment installation against drawings and schedules
Follow permit and safety procedures before work on live or isolated equipment
Update test records and progress trackers in Excel
Coordinate with vendors and contractors on site
Attend training and rotation sessions across project departments

skills.expectation: Know how motors, generators and transformers work and are rated
Recognise substation equipment such as breakers, isolators, CTs, PTs and panels
Read single line diagrams, schematics and layout drawings
Support tests such as insulation resistance and transformer checks during commissioning
Follow electrical safety practice and the CEA safety regulations (formerly IE Rules)
Make or edit electrical drawings in AutoCAD Electrical or a similar tool
Do basic load, cable sizing and earthing calculations
Keep test records, checklists and progress trackers in Excel
Report to site leads and coordinate with vendors and contractors
Work with PLC or SCADA systems in plants or substations
Simulate simple power system or machine models
Write daily site and progress reports
Help find the cause of equipment faults
